summary: Same idea and same rotating-double-cone geometry, but the port's beam is a near-zero-width ray instead of a wide soft cone (7x fewer lit pixels, 3.5x dimmer, flickering to near-black) and its hue is magenta (299 deg) where the original is crimson red (349 deg).
observations: Neither side exposes any controls (meta.json controls: [] on both; probe reports 'no settable controls' for both) - control surfaces match exactly.

Both sides compile and run clean over 60 s survey and a 40-50 s late window: no compile/runtime errors, brightnessTrend 'steady' on both, no mode/regime changes anywhere in the 60 s survey, so a single regime covers the pattern.

Shared structure (confirmed on default cloud rig, 5x5x5 lattice via --dump): both draw one spotlight double-cone whose apex sits at the volume centre, pinned bright at the centre pixel (index 62) in every frame on both sides, with the cone axis rotating in 3D.

BEAM WIDTH is the biggest divergence. Default cloud rig, per-frame counts over 26 dump times: original lights 29-41 of 125 pixels (avg 20.5 above 24/255); port lights only 3-7 (avg 2.8 above 24/255). Measuring off-axis angle of every lit pixel: the original's cone falls off smoothly out to ~40 deg off-axis (255 at core, 203 at 19 deg, 89 at 24 deg, 29 at 39 deg); EVERY lit port pixel sits at exactly 0 deg off-axis, i.e. only pixels that fall on the beam's mathematical axis light at all - the port's cone half-width is under ~25 deg where the original's is ~40 deg.

Same finding on a supplementary 24x24 grid re-render (--rig grid --grid 24x24, both sides). At t=3.0 s the original paints a band ~10 px wide across the grid (372/576 px lit, 166 above 128, brightness sum 45703); the port paints a ~4 px ribbon (152/576 lit, 68 above 128, sum 18569). At t=4.8 s the original still shows a broad diagonal band (354 lit, sum 30083) while the port is reduced to a 2x4 dot (24 lit, sum 615).

BRIGHTNESS / DROPOUT: original meanBrightness is tightly bounded 8-17 in every window (baseline, 60 s survey, 40-50 s late window), avg 11.1, and never once drops to 3 or below in 620 captured frames. The port averages 3.1-3.3 and swings 1-8: 61% of frames at <=3 and 12% at <=1, i.e. the port visibly guttering out at some beam orientations while the original holds a steady glow.

COLOR: both are single-hue with no hue animation over the whole 60 s. Original sits at hue 349 deg (crimson/red) at every dump time, saturation 0.76-1.00 - bright cores whiten toward pink ([255,171,186] at peak, [255,0,45] elsewhere). Port sits at hue 299 deg (magenta) with saturation essentially pinned at 1.00 ([249,0,255] core, all other pixels a scaled [x,0,x]). ~50 deg hue error plus a missing brightness-linked desaturation.

MOTION rate/rhythm broadly match. Both are time-based, not frame-stepped, in the same way: rendering each side at --fps 10 / 20 / 40 leaves meanBrightness unchanged (orig 11/11/11, port 3/3/3) with motion scaling inversely as expected on both, so no frame-rate coupling divergence. The 24x24 rhythm images show a comparable cadence of bright horizontal bands (~8 over 6 s on both) as the beam sweeps through the plane.

MOTION trajectory does NOT track. Measuring the beam's in-plane angle on the 24x24 grid at matched times 0-2.0 s in 0.1 s steps, the two sides' orientations differ by 7-86 deg with no constant offset (0.2 s: orig 166 deg / port 68 deg; 1.2 s: orig 163 / port 170; 1.4 s: orig 162 / port 64). Rotation SPEED is in the same ballpark on both (tens of degrees per 0.1 s), but the rotation axis/phase parameterization is not the original's.

Low-confidence caveat on defaults: this pattern has no controls at all, so the untouched-defaults comparison IS the only possible comparison - there is no dialed run to fall back on, and none is needed.

Robustness checks: an alternate seed (--seed 7, 12 s) reproduces the identical per-side means (orig 11 / port 3), so nothing here is a one-seed fluke; the late window --skip 40 --seconds 10 reproduces the same numbers, so neither side is time-degenerate.
feedback: Widen the spotlight cone. On the 5x5x5 cloud rig the original lights ~35 of 125 pixels per frame with a smooth angular falloff reaching ~40 deg off the beam axis (255 on-axis, ~200 at 19 deg, ~90 at 24 deg, ~30 at 39 deg). The port lights only 3-7, all of them exactly on-axis - its falloff is so steep that no off-axis lattice pixel ever clears zero. Target roughly a 7x increase in lit-pixel count and a falloff that still gives ~10% brightness at 40 deg.

Fix the hue: original is a fixed crimson at hue ~349 deg (R pinned at 255, B running ~35-45 above G); the port is a fixed magenta at hue ~299 deg (R == B, G == 0). Rotate the port's hue about 50 deg toward red.

Add the original's brightness-linked desaturation: the original's cone whitens toward pink as it brightens (saturation drops from 1.00 down to ~0.76, e.g. [255,171,186] in the hottest cores), while the port stays fully saturated at every level ([x,0,x] everywhere).

Eliminate the port's brightness dropouts. The original's frame mean never leaves 8-17 across 620 frames in three separate windows; the port swings 1-8 and sits at or below 1 for 12% of frames, so it appears to blink out at certain beam orientations. Once the cone is widened this may resolve on its own - the dropouts coincide with orientations where the thin ray misses all lattice pixels - but confirm the frame mean stops dipping.

Lower priority: the rotation SPEED and rhythm cadence already match (both ~8 in-plane sweeps per 6 s, both time-based rather than frame-stepped), but the orientation trajectory does not track the original's at matched times (7-86 deg apart with no constant offset), so the rotation axis/phase parameterization differs. Not viewer-visible on its own; fix only after the cone and colour.
